one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: A fully integrated home-textile manufacturer producing curtain and upholstery fabrics, readymade curtains and fabric-processing (job-work) services, selling under own brands and on private/white-label basis.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Harit Industries Limited operates as a fully integrated textile manufacturing entity in the Home Textile Sector, managing the entire value chain in-house from design to weaving, processing and finishing. It runs three core divisions - fabrics for curtains and upholstery, fabric processing on a job-work basis (primarily dyeing, plus embroidery and weaving), and readymade curtains - across economy and premium price points. Customers are wholesalers, retailers and corporate customers for the curtain/fabric divisions and textile manufacturers for the job-work division; through its Subsidiaries the Company also trades yarn and greige fabric.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- Harit Fabtex (India) Private Limited — Family-owned textile business; other directorship of Non-Executive Director Chandrakant Ramswaroop Mishra: Engaged in manufacture of greige curtain fabrics; Promoter Pankaj Mishra was an Executive Director, resigned in 2022 and transferred his shareholding, exiting completely
- Jai Bhavani Furnishing Private Limited — Former venture of Promoter Pankaj Mishra: Engaged in marketing and distribution of curtain fabrics across India; he became shareholder and Executive Director in 2012, resigned from directorship in 2020 and transferred shareholding, exiting completely
- JB Decor — Proprietorship concern founded by Promoter Devyani Pankaj Mishra (2012 to 2019): Engaged in trading of curtain fabrics
- Harit Concepts Private Limited — Other directorship of Promoters Pankaj Mishra and Devyani Mishra
- Daphne Multitrading Private Limited — Other directorship of Promoters Pankaj Mishra and Devyani Mishra
- Krishna Fancyfab Private Limited — Other directorship of Promoters Pankaj Mishra and Devyani Mishra
- Sangeeta Texdyes Private Limited — Other directorship of Promoters Pankaj Mishra and Devyani Mishra
- Golddust Credit Capitals Limited — Other directorship of Promoter Devyani Mishra and Non-Executive Director Chandrakant Ramswaroop Mishra
- Sarjai Investment and Finance Private Limited — Other directorship of Promoter Devyani Mishra
- Pandit Ramswaroop Mishra Seva Foundation — Other directorship of Promoter Pankaj Mishra and Non-Executive Director Chandrakant Ramswaroop Mishra
- Eleven Point Two Fintech Private Limited — Other directorship of Independent Director Rajesh Bhalchandra Dhume
- Subsidiaries (not named in the routed sections) — Subsidiaries of the Company: Engaged in trading of yarn and greige fabric; majority of such revenue generated in the state of Maharashtra

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Fully integrated (backward and forward) textile manufacturing: the Company manages the entire value chain in-house — from design to weaving, processing and finishing. Two mutually exclusive raw-material routes are used: (i) yarn is procured externally and undergoes the complete in-house process — weaving, dyeing, finishing and conversion into the final product; or (ii) greige fabric is procured directly, bypassing the weaving stage and entering the dyeing process, followed by embroidery / printing and final finishing. Stage 1 is raw material procurement (greige / yarn); Stage 2 is weaving (jacquard/dobby/greige), dyeing, embroidery and print; Stage 3 is packing, cutting and finishing, with cut, roll and readymade warehouses feeding customer dispatch. The embroidery and dyeing process involves two cycles — greige fabric is first sent to the dyeing unit for initial coloration, then to the embroidery unit for machine embroidery, then back to the dyeing unit for final dyeing and finishing, then back to embroidery for quality checks before dispatch to the Kalher warehouse; for jacquard and dobby fabrics the material goes directly from dyeing to the warehouse for dispatch. Weaving is performed on pre-owned Thema Super Excel Loom machines; dyeing uses jigger dyeing, jet dyeing, mercerizing, sanforising, decadising and hot air stenters; embroidery uses computerized multi-head machines with CAD; printing uses digital printers and heat transfer printing machines. In addition to in-house weaving the Company also procures selected greige fabric from third-party suppliers. The DRHP describes the September 2025 acquisition of a fabric processing unit from Aloka Exports (land, building and machinery) for ₹1,951 Lakhs as forming part of the Company's capacity expansion and forward integration strategy. The Company cautions that because it follows a forward-integrated model, reported production figures may reflect overlapping quantities since output from one stage is input to the next, and include internal consumption.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Revenue mix shift towards fabric processing (job work), which rose from 32.95% of revenue from operations in Fiscal 2023 to 46.08% in Fiscal 2024, 49.49% in Fiscal 2025 and 51.58% in the six months ended September 30, 2025, while fabrics for curtain and upholstery fell from 45.31% to 31.99% over Fiscal 2023 to Fiscal 2025
- Within the job-work division the customer supplies the fabric, so the cost base is consumables (coal, chemicals, colours) rather than raw material, whereas the manufacturing divisions carry yarn and greige fabric input cost
- Mix within curtain and upholstery fabric has shifted to economy from premium: premium SKU revenue fell from Rs 935.36 Lakhs in Fiscal 2023 to Rs 354.51 Lakhs in Fiscal 2025 while economy revenue was Rs 3,726.28 Lakhs and Rs 3,766.79 Lakhs respectively
- Seasonality of the design cycle: new designs launch in June / July, so first-half SKU counts are structurally lower (5,736 fabric SKUs in H1 FY26 versus 9,060 in Fiscal 2025)
- Geographic concentration in Maharashtra, which contributed 71.23% of revenue from operations in Fiscal 2025 and 69.15% in the six months ended September 30, 2025
- Supplier and customer concentration: top 10 suppliers contributed 64.49% of purchases and top 10 customers 29.24% of revenue in Fiscal 2025
- Order-book model based on purchase orders and job-work assignments with an average lead time for order delivery of 4-6 weeks
- Declining contribution from the subsidiary-level yarn and greige fabric trading line, from 12.29% of revenue from operations in Fiscal 2024 to 8.00% in Fiscal 2025 and 1.74% in the six months ended September 30, 2025

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Launch new sets of designs every calendar year in June / July, with SKUs sold expected to increase by the end of Fiscal 2026 on new launches
- Continue to operate an integrated in-house model across design, weaving, processing and finishing rather than outsourcing stages of the value chain
- Deleverage the balance sheet by repaying / pre-paying certain outstanding borrowings out of the Net Proceeds
- Use the NSE EMERGE listing to enhance visibility and brand image among existing and potential customers, create a public market for the Equity Shares in India and lower financing costs

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The routed sections describe no new plant, line or capacity-addition project. The stated growth path is organic within the existing Maharashtra-based integrated units: the Company was engaged in curtain and upholstery fabrics since incorporation in 2019 and expanded from 2020 into fabric-processing job work for third parties, and it now offers integrated operations across readymade curtains, fabrics for curtains and upholstery, and fabric processing. Product-side expansion is via a new design collection launched each June / July, with the SKU count expected to rise by the end of Fiscal 2026. The Issue proceeds are earmarked for debt repayment and general corporate purposes, not for capacity expansion. Manufacturing and finishing / warehousing facilities remain concentrated in Maharashtra.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Fully integrated in-house value chain from design to weaving, dyeing, stitching, processing and finishing, which the DRHP states leads to faster production cycles with efficiency and a competitive edge
- Presence across both economy and premium price points in curtain/upholstery fabrics and readymade curtains, sold under own brands as well as on private and white-labelling basis
- Two owned brands - 'The Home' (premium, Rs 100-800 per metre) and 'NM Homes' (economy, Rs 100-300 per metre) - each targeted at distinct customer segments and price points
- Broad SKU range: 9,060 curtain and upholstery fabric SKUs and 569 readymade curtain SKUs sold in Fiscal 2025
- Pan-India distribution footprint across 16 states with revenue from curtain and upholstery fabrics spread across the country
- Three complementary revenue streams (own-product manufacturing, third-party job work and subsidiary-level trading) with short average order lead time of 4-6 weeks
- Restated Consolidated Financial Statements contain no auditor qualification requiring adjustments

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Geographic concentration in Maharashtra for both revenue and assets — Maharashtra contributed 69.15%, 71.23%, 68.12% and 58.13% of revenue for H1 FY26 and Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023; manufacturing and finishing / warehousing facilities are also concentrated in the state, so a single-state disruption hits revenue and production simultaneously
- Supplier concentration, compounded by the supplier base itself sitting in Maharashtra — Top 10 suppliers contributed 61.07%, 64.49%, 56.93% and 53.02% for H1 FY26 and Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023; raw material and stores/consumables sourcing is concentrated in the same state as operations
- Customer concentration without long-term agreements — Top 10 customers contributed 32.43%, 29.24%, 24.15% and 27.52% for H1 FY26 and Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023; the Company states it does not have long-term agreements with such customers
- Raw material and consumable price volatility — Yarn and greige fabric are the key inputs for the manufacturing divisions and coal, chemicals and colours for job work; the DRHP flags that increases or fluctuations may adversely impact pricing and supply
- Dependence on corporate and wholesale clients in home textiles and furnishings — 28.17%, 25.18%, 27.87% and 34.47% of manufacturing revenue came from corporate and wholesale clients for H1 FY26 and Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023; changes in their business models or procurement policies would reduce revenue
- Fast-fashion demand and consumer-preference risk in the home textile / curtain segment — The Company describes its segment as a fast fashion fabric solution vulnerable to variations in demand and changes in consumer preferences
- Historical corporate-compliance defects — The DRHP discloses inadvertent inconsistencies in historical corporate filings, and a past preferential issue where subscription monies were not kept in a separate bank account as prescribed under the Companies Act; a compounding application has been filed and penalties may be imposed
- Reliance on issuer-commissioned secondary industry data — Industry information is drawn from the Ken Research Report commissioned and paid for by the Company exclusively for the Issue, which the DRHP itself flags as subject to inherent risks

commitments.title: Promises (RHP)
commitments.body:
- **Utilise Rs 5,248.00 Lakhs of the Net Proceeds towards repayment / pre-payment, in full or in part, of certain outstanding loans availed by the Company, with the entire amount deployed in Fiscal 2027.**
- **Raise a fresh Issue aggregating up to Rs 7,000.00 Lakhs by the Company, listed on NSE EMERGE.**
- **Cap General Corporate Purposes at the lower of 15% of the Gross Proceeds of the Issue or Rs 1,000.00 Lakhs.**
- **Curtain and upholstery fabric SKUs sold are expected to increase by the end of Fiscal 2026 on the back of the new design sets launched each June / July (5,736 SKUs sold in the six months ended September 30, 2025 versus 9,060 in Fiscal …**
- **Launch new sets of designs every calendar year in the month of June / July across the curtain and upholstery fabric range.**
- **Use the NSE EMERGE listing to enhance visibility and brand image among existing and potential customers, create a public market for the Equity Shares in India, lower financing costs and deliver better value to investors.**
- **Continue to disclose all KPIs included in the MD&A section on a periodic basis, at least once a year, for one year after listing or till complete utilisation of the Fresh Issue proceeds.**
- **Management flags that a past preferential issue where subscription monies were not maintained in a separate bank account as prescribed under the Companies Act may attract penalties; a compounding application has been filed.**
- **Management flags inadvertent inconsistencies in certain historical corporate filings which may result in penalties or fines being imposed by the competent regulatory authority.**
- **A subsidiary has received a notice under the Income-tax Act, 1961 for Assessment Year 2019-20 and reassessment proceedings have been initiated; management believes no material liability is expected and has made no provision, disclosing it …**
